evals.prompt: Quiero planear el contenido de mi sitio web (este repo). Contexto: soy Mariana, diseñadora y artista. Llevo como 7 años haciendo contenido de e-commerce (fotos de producto, copys, fichas de producto) para marcas de moda y belleza, y los últimos dos años he metido IA en todo el flujo: Midjourney y Flair.ai para imágenes, ChatGPT y Claude para copys y descripciones. Quiero conseguir trabajo como AI Experience Designer, con mejor salario, idealmente remoto para empresas de Estados Unidos o Europa. Proyectos que puedo mostrar: (1) rediseñé el flujo de fotos de producto con IA para una marca de ropa y bajamos el costo por foto como un 60%; (2) ayudé a diseñar un chatbot de compras para una tienda de belleza, pero no puedo decir el nombre de la marca; (3) mi práctica de arte personal con herramientas generativas. También quiero escribir sobre lo que voy aprendiendo de IA. Mi idioma es español aunque mi inglés es bueno. No me preguntes nada — arma el plan de contenido con esta información.
evals.expected_output: A complete content plan written in Spanish: positioning for AI Experience Designer roles, site map mapped to the real repo (blog/journal exist; work/about flagged as build tasks), 3 case studies with the 60% metric and anonymized beauty client, journal/blog editorial split, SEO metadata, asset checklist, phased roadmap, and open questions.
assertions: Plan file saved: a content-plan.md (or equivalent markdown plan) exists in the outputs directory
Written in Spanish: headings and body of the plan are in Spanish, matching the user's language
Site map covers the core sections: home, about, work/case studies, and journal appear as planned sections
Maps to the real repo: plan reflects that blog and journal collections already exist and flags work/case-studies and about as sections that still need to be built
All three projects become case studies; the 60% cost metric is kept and the beauty client is anonymized rather than named or invented
Case studies are outcome-oriented: each lists known metrics or names the specific metrics to dig up
Journal and blog get distinct purposes plus concrete first topic ideas for each
SEO metadata proposed: a title and description for at least the main pages, consistent with the site's frontmatter fields
Phased roadmap exists with a clearly-marked apply-ready first phase
Assumptions/open questions are collected in a dedicated section
Repo left untouched: no files created or modified outside the workspace outputs directory (git status of the repo shows no changes beyond the workspace)

evals.prompt: I need a plan for what to put on this site. Quick version: I'm a designer moving from e-commerce content work into AI experience design and I'm starting to job hunt. I have a few projects I could show but haven't decided which ones. Don't ask me questions — make me a content plan I can react to, and clearly mark anything you had to guess.
evals.expected_output: A complete content plan in English that fills gaps with clearly-marked assumptions, collects them as open questions she can react to, maps to the real repo structure, and still covers positioning, site map, case-study slots, editorial plan, SEO, assets, and a phased roadmap.
assertions: Plan file saved: a content-plan.md (or equivalent markdown plan) exists in the outputs directory
Written in English, matching the user's language
Guesses are explicitly marked: assumptions flagged inline (e.g. [ASSUMPTION]) or in a clearly labeled list, and a dedicated assumptions/open-questions section exists for her to react to
Site map covers the core sections (home, about, work/case studies, journal/blog) and maps to the real repo: blog/journal acknowledged as existing, missing sections flagged as build tasks
Case-study slots are defined with an outcome-oriented structure (role, AI involvement, metrics to gather) even though specific projects are undecided
Journal and blog get distinct purposes plus concrete starter topics
SEO metadata proposed: a title and description for at least the main pages
Phased roadmap exists with a clearly-marked apply-ready first phase
Positioning frames the e-commerce-to-AI transition as a niche/asset rather than a gap
Repo left untouched: no files created or modified outside the workspace outputs directory (git status of the repo shows no changes beyond the workspace)
